answer: S/Kademlia-style prefix binding ties each agent ID to the network block it calls from. First, the agent hashes its public key with its /24 IPv4 prefix to derive its ID. Second, peers drop any ID whose prefix doesn't match the address they actually see. Third, the ledger caps each /24 at two IDs, so a farm pushing traffic through one narrow inlet gets two seats, not two hundred. Running 100 fakes needs 50 separate /24 blocks at about $150 a month each to lease, so $7,500 monthly, or near $12,000 per block to buy. Picture an orchard that tags each tree, not each velvet-skinned peach.
